skill.name: cloud-claw-launch-agent
skill.description: Launch new AltClaw, OpenClaw, PicoClaw, or Ottie deployments through Cloud Claw using local AltLLM CLI commands. It covers launch fields, allowed values, tokens, models, and quota checks.
skill.summary: Guides safe creation of new Cloud Claw agent deployments with the local AltLLM CLI.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick detections are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, but the documented deployment command is real. The parent-directory references are confirmed because they direct the agent outside the reviewed skill package. Semantic review found cost-bearing deployment risk that requires explicit confirmation and careful secret handling.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory references leave the reviewed skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Move required shared guidance into the skill package or replace parent paths with reviewed marketplace resources.

remediation.issue: The launch workflow can create cloud resources and consume account capacity.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation of name, agent type, model, cost impact, quota, and account state before deployment.

remediation.issue: Launches require sensitive token inputs for some agent types.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or secure files for tokens, and state that raw secrets must be redacted from chat and logs.

content.value_statement: Cloud Claw deployments require correct agent choices, names, tokens, and quota checks. This skill guides new launches through the local AltLLM CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guides only the new Cloud Claw deployment workflow.
Maps OpenClaw, PicoClaw, and Ottie to internal agent type values.
Applies name, agent type, model, and Telegram token constraints.
Surfaces quota, free slot, credit, and payment prerequisites before launch.
Points users to expected launch responses and common failure states.
limitations: Does not start, stop, delete, or inspect existing deployments.
Requires the local AltLLM CLI, authentication, and account access.
Cannot bypass quota, credits, free slots, or payment requirements.
Requires users to provide valid secrets through safe local inputs.

best_practices: Confirm deployment name, agent type, model, and cost impact before running the launch command.
Use environment variables or secure files for tokens, and redact secrets from chat history.
Check account quota, credits, and free-slot status before starting a launch.
anti_patterns: Running a deployment before the user confirms final parameters.
Pasting raw Telegram or API tokens directly into chat.
Using this skill to manage existing deployments after launch.

faq.question: What does this skill launch?
faq.answer: It launches new Cloud Claw deployments for OpenClaw, PicoClaw, and Ottie agent types.

faq.question: Can it manage existing deployments?
faq.answer: No. It is limited to new launch workflows and does not handle start, stop, delete, or logs.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it need secrets?
faq.answer: Some launches require a Telegram bot token. Use environment variables or secure files instead of raw chat text.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a successful launch?
faq.answer: No. Success depends on authentication, quota, credits, payment state, free slots, and valid inputs.

faq.question: Should users confirm before deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should review final parameters and account impact before any deployment command runs.
